facts.text: The README warns to keep away from the robot arm to avoid personal injury or equipment damage and to make a safety assessment before moving to prevent collisions
Robot type XARM7_X4 has the number 7
The SDK parses the axis count, the robot type and the firmware version out of the controller's version string (axis, device_type, version_number)

The SDK picks the joint range table of an arm by its axis count and robot type, and the table numbered <axis>1305 (71305 for 7 axes) when characters 3 to 6 of the serial number are from 1305 to below 8500
The 1305 table of the 7-axis type XARM7_X4 narrows joint 2 to -2.042035..2.024581 rad and joint 4 to -0.10472..3.92699 rad
The SDK's own joint range check is on by default (check_joint_limit) and covers set_servo_angle and set_servo_angle_j
The SDK's own TCP range check is off by default (check_tcp_limit) and documented to check only roll, pitch and yaw, so the position ranges of TCP_LIMITS are not checked by it
Every API call returns a code: 0 is success, a negative code is an SDK-side failure and a positive code comes from the controller or the protocol

The controller reports error 1 when its Emergency Stop Button is pushed, 2 when the Emergency IO of the Control Box is triggered and 3 when the Emergency Stop Button of the Three-state Switch is pressed
emergency_stop() sets state 4 (stop) and repeats it every 0.1 s for up to 3 s until the controller reports state 4
The wrapper documents emergency_stop as set_state(4), motion_enable(True), set_state(0) and says it does not clear an error
set_state selects the motion state (0), pause (3), stop (4) or deceleration stop (6)
clean_error is documented to need motion enabled (motion_enable(True)) and state 0 set (set_state(state=0)) by hand after it
clean_warn cleans the warnings and returns an API code
motion_enable takes enable True or False and a servo_id of 1 to the number of axes, or None
The upstream xArm 7 move example enables motion, then sets mode 0 and state 0, before it moves
Joint velocity control needs joint velocity control mode (set_mode(4)) and, in the upstream example, set_state(0) after it
Watchdog of a velocity command: over its duration (seconds) the arm sets the speed to 0 by itself (firmware 1.8.0 or newer); a duration of 0 or less never stops it
An arm with firmware older than 1.8.0 is sent -1 instead of the duration, and -1 is equivalent to 0, which never stops
The SDK's speed ranges for position moves are 0.1 to 1000 mm/s for the tool and 0.0001 to 4.0 rad/s for the joints
A move that names no speed runs at the last used speed: 100 mm/s (tool) and 20 deg/s (joints) after start
